title: Affine finite presentation of the automorphism functor of a finite projective module
statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative ring and let $P$ be an $A$-module which is a direct summand of $A^n$ for some finite $n\geq0$. For a commutative $A$-algebra $B$ put $P_B=B\otimes_A P$ [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. The functor $B\mapsto\operatorname{Aut}_B(P_B)$, with multiplication given by composition and transition maps given by scalar extension, is represented by an affine $\operatorname{Spec}A$-group scheme $\operatorname{GL}_A(P)$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. It is finitely presented over $A$, and its identity section is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion] defined by a finitely generated ideal in its coordinate algebra. More explicitly, for any split maps $i:P\to A^n$, $p:A^n\to P$ with $pi=1_P$, put $e=ip\in\operatorname{Mat}_n(A)$. A representing coordinate algebra is
$$D_e=A[u_{ij},v_{ij}:1\leq i,j\leq n]/(eU-U,Ue-U,eV-V,Ve-V,UV-e,VU-e),$$
where $U=(u_{ij})$, $V=(v_{ij})$, and each matrix relation denotes all its entries. The representing bijection sends an automorphism $a$ of $P_B$ to $(i_Bap_B,i_Ba^{-1}p_B)$. The identity section sends both matrices to $e$; its ideal is generated by the entries of $U-e$ and $V-e$. For every ring homomorphism $A\to A'$ the canonical isomorphism $\operatorname{GL}_A(P)\times_{\operatorname{Spec}A}\operatorname{Spec}A'\cong\operatorname{GL}_{A'}(A'\otimes_A P)$ identifies an automorphism with its scalar extension and identifies the two identity sections. These identifications commute with successive base changes. The statements include $P=0$, $n=0$, the zero ring, and projective modules of varying rank.

source.place: Tag 022W, example-general-linear-group, the finite-free representing matrix scheme. The direct-summand idempotent matrix presentation and finite identity ideal are an agent-supplied extension; their full construction is in the Q31 report.

proof.text: Fix the split maps in the statement. On pure tensors define $i_B(b\otimes x)=b\otimes i(x)$ and $p_B(b\otimes z)=b\otimes p(z)$. The tensor universal property gives these maps and $p_Bi_B=1$. Identify $B\otimes_A A^n$ with $B^n$ by $b\otimes(a_j)_j\mapsto(b a_j)_j$, with inverse $(b_j)_j\mapsto\sum_j b_j\otimes\delta_j$. Thus $e_B=i_Bp_B$ is the entrywise image of $e$, and $e_B^2=e_B$. Every identity here holds on pure tensors, which generate the tensor product. No flatness or constant rank is used.

source.place: Tag 022W, example-general-linear-group; agent extension from the free case to a supplied split summand, by the explicit matrix calculations below.

proof.text: Put $T=A[u_{ij},v_{ij}]$ and let $I$ be the ideal generated by the six families of entries displayed in the statement. Evaluation gives a bijection between $A$-algebra maps $T\to B$ and matrix pairs $(U,V)$ over $B$. Such a map factors uniquely through $D_e=T/I$ exactly when all six relations vanish: define the factor on a coset by $t+I\mapsto f(t)$; this is well defined precisely when $I\subseteq\ker(f)$. Consequently $\operatorname{Hom}_{A\text{-alg}}(D_e,B)$ is naturally the set of these pairs. Naturality is entrywise application of the algebra map.

source.place: Tag 022W, example-general-linear-group; agent extension from the free case to a supplied split summand, by the explicit matrix calculations below.

proof.text: For $a\in\operatorname{Aut}_B(P_B)$ put $U=i_Bap_B$, $V=i_Ba^{-1}p_B$. Substitution using $p_Bi_B=1$ gives $e_BU=Ue_B=U$, $e_BV=Ve_B=V$, and $UV=VU=e_B$. Conversely, a solution pair gives $a=p_BUi_B$ and $a'=p_BVi_B$. Their products are $aa'=p_BUe_BVi_B=p_BUVi_B=p_Be_Bi_B=1$ and $a'a=1$ by the reversed calculation. Finally $i_B(p_BUi_B)p_B=e_BUe_B=U$, and likewise for $V$, while $p_B(i_Bap_B)i_B=a$. These formulas prove the two constructions are inverse. Scalar extension applies the algebra map to every matrix entry, hence respects both constructions.

source.place: Tag 022W, example-general-linear-group; agent extension from the free case to a supplied split summand, by the explicit matrix calculations below.

proof.text: Let $G=\operatorname{Spec}D_e$ with its structure map to $S=\operatorname{Spec}A$. The affine-spectrum correspondence identifies $S$-maps $\operatorname{Spec}B\to G$ with the $A$-algebra maps of step 2, so step 3 gives the required natural representing bijection. Both $G$ and $S$ are affine, so $G\to S$ is an affine morphism by [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-affine-schemes-affine].

source.place: Tag 022W, example-general-linear-group; agent extension from the free case to a supplied split summand, by the explicit matrix calculations below.

proof.text: The fibre product $G\times_S G$ has coordinate algebra $D_e\otimes_A D_e$. In it denote the two universal pairs by $(U_1,V_1)$ and $(U_2,V_2)$. Define multiplication by the algebra map $U\mapsto U_1U_2$, $V\mapsto V_2V_1$. It respects the relations: $eU_1U_2=U_1U_2=U_1U_2e$, and $(U_1U_2)(V_2V_1)=U_1eV_1=e$, with the reversed product and the support relations for $V_2V_1$ proved identically. Define inverse by swapping $U,V$ and identity by $U,V\mapsto e$. These also respect all relations since $e^2=e$. The affine-spectrum correspondence gives scheme morphisms. Associativity follows on generators from $(U_1U_2)U_3=U_1(U_2U_3)$ and the reversed formula for $V$; the identity and inverse diagrams follow from $eU=Ue=U$, $eV=Ve=V$, and $UV=VU=e$. The algebra maps out of $D_e\otimes_AD_e$ and $D_e\otimes_AD_e\otimes_AD_e$ needed for these diagrams (such as $m^*\otimes1$) are the tensor-product maps of [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property] (2), and maps out of $D_e$ agreeing on the generators are equal; equality of algebra maps is equality of scheme maps. Thus this is a group scheme. Step 3 sends composition $a_1a_2$ to $(U_1U_2,V_2V_1)$, so it represents the group-valued functor with the specified multiplication.

source.place: Tag 022W, example-general-linear-group; agent extension from the free case to a supplied split summand, by the explicit matrix calculations below.

proof.text: There are $2n^2$ variables and $6n^2$ specified relation entries, so $D_e$ is a finitely presented $A$-algebra by definition. The whole affine source and target witness local finite presentation at every source point. The affine morphism in step 4 is quasi-compact and quasi-separated by affine-morphism permanence (3). Together these are precisely finite presentation of the scheme morphism.

Let $J\subseteq D_e$ be generated by the $2n^2$ entries of $U-e$ and $V-e$. Evaluation at $(e,e)$ gives an $A$-algebra map $\epsilon:D_e\to A$, and $J\subseteq\ker\epsilon$. In $D_e/J$ every variable is its prescribed entry of $e$, so the structure map $A\to D_e/J$ is surjective. Evaluation descends and is its inverse, since the composites fix $A$ and all the generators. Therefore $D_e/J\cong A$, $\ker\epsilon=J$, and the identity section is the quotient-spectrum closed immersion with this finitely generated ideal.

source.place: Tag 01IG, example-closed-immersion-affines; the identity kernel is computed explicitly here

proof.text: For $A\to A'$ use $i'=1\otimes i$, $p'=1\otimes p$; step 1 gives $p'i'=1$ and the projector $e'$ obtained entrywise from $e$. Write $D_{e'}$ for the same presentation over $A'$. Define $A'\otimes_A D_e\to D_{e'}$ by $a'\otimes f(U,V)\mapsto a'f(U',V')$ with coefficients mapped to $A'$. Evaluation factors through the relations, and the $A$-algebra map out of the tensor product is given by [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property] (2) from $A'\to D_{e'}$ and this evaluation. Its inverse sends $U',V'$ to $1\otimes U,1\otimes V$ and $a'$ to $a'\otimes1$; these satisfy exactly the displayed relations with $e'$. Both composites fix coefficients and generators, hence are identity by the uniqueness clause (3) of that node and the polynomial universal property. The fibre-product formula and affine-spectrum correspondence now give $G\times_S\operatorname{Spec}A'\cong\operatorname{Spec}D_{e'}$. On points its matrices are those of the same automorphism under $B\otimes_{A'}(A'\otimes_A P)\cong B\otimes_A P$, $b\otimes(a'\otimes x)\mapsto ba'\otimes x$, whose inverse sends $b\otimes x$ to $b\otimes(1\otimes x)$. Thus the isomorphism identifies scalar extension, the group laws in step 5, and identity evaluation.

source.place: Tag 022W, example-general-linear-group; agent extension from the free case to a supplied split summand, by the explicit matrix calculations below.

proof.text: For a further map $A'\to A''$, both the iterated and direct coordinate-algebra identifications send each of $U,V$ to its identically named variable over $A''$ and send coefficients along $A\to A''$, so they coincide. The iterated tensor comparison sends $b\otimes(a''\otimes(a'\otimes x))$ to $ba''a'\otimes x$ in either order. Identity matrices go to $e''$ in both cases. This also makes the representing scheme independent, up to its unique functor-compatible isomorphism, of the chosen splitting: between two presentations send universal matrices to $\tilde i\,pUi\,\tilde p$ and $\tilde i\,pVi\,\tilde p$ (all maps extended to the relevant universal algebra); step 3 proves these changes are inverse and preserve the represented automorphism. If $n=0$ the polynomial ring is $A$, there are no relations or generators of $J$, and $P=0$. If $P=0$ with $n>0$, then $e=0$ and the support equations force $U=V=0$, again giving $D_e=A$ and $J=0$. For the zero ring all rings in the presentations are zero and the group functor on its algebras is trivial. The calculations nowhere impose constant rank, so varying-rank projective modules are included.
